title: Auto Body Marketing: How Shops Get More Estimates (2026)
summary: Auto body marketing and advertising for shop owners: what the ads show, channels that bring estimates, example copy, and how to measure cost per job.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Auto body marketing works when it reaches a driver at the moment of damage, or a driver who is tired of living with it, and offers a free estimate as the one next step.
- Two buyers need two messages: the person who just had a wreck and wants it handled, and the person with old dents, faded paint or rust who keeps putting it off.
- Best channels: Google Search, a complete Google Business Profile, Meta ads for the put-it-off buyer, and referral relationships with tow operators and insurers.
- Measure cost per estimate and cost per booked repair, then compare it with gross profit per job.


## Auto body customers arrive in two very different ways


Most auto body advertising fails because it talks to everyone. A driver standing next to a crumpled bumper has one question: who can fix this and how fast. A driver with a dented door from three years ago has a different question: is it worth the hassle. The first buyer searches. The second buyer has to be interrupted.


After a wreck Living with the damage


Situation Recent collision, often with an insurance claim open Old dents, scratches, faded clear coat, spreading rust


How they find you Google Search, maps, a tow operator or insurer referral A Facebook or Instagram ad, a neighbor, a drive-by


Decision speed Hours to days Weeks to months


What wins the job Fast answer, reviews, easy drop-off, help with the claim Before and after photos, a free estimate, a clear price range


Best next step Call now or book a time to bring the car in Send photos for an estimate or book a short visit


Write one ad for each buyer. Do not try to cover both in the same headline.


## What the live auto body ads show


The[auto body ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/auto-body-ads) collects 45 live Meta ads from 12 advertisers. That is a small set, so read it for patterns and not as a benchmark. The most common call to action on the page is Book now. The typical ad has run 80 days, which is under three months. Six of the ads shown have run well past that, from 407 days up to 1,938 days, or more than five years.


The ads that keep running share a few traits:


- **They say who the shop is and where it is.** One long-runner opens with "Family-owned and operated auto body shop in Bozeman, MT!" Another opens with "Family Owned & Operated Since 1937" and has run 427 days as a video. Local ownership and a place name come first.
- **They list services in one plain line.** Several of the oldest ads open with a list: collision repair, mechanical work, upholstery, tires, towing. The driver learns in one glance that the shop can handle the whole problem.
- **They speak to the accident directly.** One ad that has run 420 days opens by asking if the driver had an accident and tells them to relax. It names the situation and the reassurance, nothing else.
- **They do not lead with a discount.** The openers are about trust and capability. The offer shows up in the button and the body copy.


The pattern is not clever creative. It is a local shop stating what it does, who owns it and how to reach it, and leaving the ad running while it keeps producing calls.


## Channels that bring auto body leads


1. **Google Search.** The highest-intent channel for the post-wreck buyer. Target terms such as "collision repair near me", "auto body shop \[city\]", "bumper repair" and "paint repair". Add your town to the ad copy and to the landing page headline.
2. **Google Business Profile.** Many drivers choose from the map results without clicking an ad. Keep hours, photos of finished repairs and the phone number current, and ask every happy customer for a review at pickup. Our[auto repair marketing guide](https://www.sprites.ai/auto-repair-marketing) covers the profile basics that apply to both trades.
3. **Google Local Services Ads.** Pay-per-lead listings at the top of local results. Eligibility depends on the service category and your area, so check Google's list before you plan around it. The[Local Services Ads guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) explains setup.
4. **Facebook and Instagram.** The best way to reach the driver who keeps putting it off. Show a dented fender next to the repaired one, name the neighborhood, and offer a free estimate by photo.
5. **Referral partners.** Tow operators, rental counters, insurance agents and mechanics who do not do body work all see damaged cars before you do. A short visit and a reliable turnaround time earns referrals that cost nothing per click. Roofers work the same way with insurance claims, which our[roofing marketing guide](https://www.sprites.ai/roofing-marketing) describes.


## Auto body advertising examples you can adapt


### Google Search ad for the post-wreck driver


Responsive search ads allow headlines up to 30 characters and descriptions up to 90 characters. A set for a collision shop:


Element Copy Characters


Headline 1 Collision Repair in Tampa 25


Headline 2 Free Collision Estimates 24


Headline 3 Photo Estimate in Minutes 25


Headline 4 Paint Matched to Your Car 25


Description 1 Family-owned collision shop. Free written estimate, honest repair plan, and a warranty. 87


Description 2 Dents, scratches, rust and collision damage. Send photos or book a time to drop off. 84


Only promise a warranty and a turnaround if your shop honors them in writing.


### Meta ad for the driver who keeps putting it off


**Image:** a split photo of the same door before and after, same angle and light. **Primary text:** "That dent has been there long enough. Send us two photos and we will give you a free estimate, including the rust spot you have been ignoring. Most estimates come back the same day." **Headline:** "Stop living with the damage." **Button:** Get quote or Book now.


### Video ad


A 20 to 30 second walk around one car: arrival, the damage up close, the finished panel, the owner picking up the keys. Open with the shop's name and town in the first line of text. One of the longest-running ads on the wall is a video that leads with how long the family has owned the shop.


## Make the free estimate easy to claim


The offer in nearly every strong auto body ad is a free collision estimate. What separates a good one from a weak one is how little effort it takes to claim.


- Offer a photo estimate: the driver sends four pictures by text or a form and gets a range back.
- Offer a drop-off time, not just a phone number. Book now works because it asks for a specific action.
- Say what is included: written estimate, paint match, rust treatment, a loaner or rental help if you offer it.
- Answer calls and forms fast. A driver with an undriveable car will call the next shop if yours goes to voicemail.


## The math: what an estimate is worth


These numbers are an example. Replace them with your own.


Line Example


Monthly ad spend $1,500


Estimate requests 30


Cost per estimate request $50


Requests that bring the car in 50%, or 15 visits


Visits that become repairs 60%, or 9 jobs


Cost per booked repair About $167


Average repair ticket $3,200


Gross profit at 40% $1,280 per job, $11,520 for 9 jobs


In this example the shop pays about $167 to win a job that earns $1,280 in gross profit. If the close rate fell to 20%, the shop would win 3 jobs and pay $500 each. That still clears the margin, but the picture changes fast, which is why the close rate matters as much as the cost per lead.


## How to measure auto body marketing


Track four numbers each month: estimate requests by source, cars that arrived, repairs booked, and revenue per repair. Use a tracked phone number for each channel so you can tell Google calls from Meta calls. Ask every caller how they found you and log it. A channel with cheap leads and a low close rate can lose to a channel with fewer leads that book more often.


Insurance work and cash work often carry different margins. Tag each job as one or the other so you can see which ads bring the jobs you want. For more trade patterns across local businesses, see[local business ads](https://www.sprites.ai/local-business-ads) .

## FAQ


### What is the best auto body marketing strategy?


Start with Google Search and a complete Google Business Profile to catch drivers who need a shop now. Add Facebook and Instagram ads with before and after photos for drivers who have been putting repairs off. Offer a free estimate in both.


### How do auto body shops get more leads?


They show up when someone searches after a wreck, collect reviews at every pickup, run photo-based ads for old damage, and build referral ties with tow operators and insurance agents. Fast answers to calls and forms keep the leads they pay for.


### What should an auto body ad say?


Say who you are and where you are, what you fix, and what the driver does next. The longest-running ads on the[auto body ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/auto-body-ads) open with family ownership, a town name or a plain list of services, then offer a free estimate or a booking.


### Do Facebook ads work for auto body shops?


They can, mostly for cosmetic work and for drivers who have lived with damage for a while. Use clear before and after images, name your area and make the estimate easy to request. Judge them by cost per booked repair, not clicks.


### How much should an auto body shop spend on advertising?


Work backward from the job. Find your gross profit per repair, your close rate on estimates, and how many estimates you need for one job. Spend more on channels where the cost per booked repair stays well under the profit per repair.
